claude.request:
Today's international headlines:
- Russia's offensive ability is broken, Kyiv's former top general tells BBC: In his first interview since being forced from his post, Gen Syrskyi speaks about Ukraine's future in the war.
- One dead and several hurt after rollercoaster incident at Six Flags: Aerial footage at the park after the incident shows a stuck rollercoaster with riders being helped off.
- Breaking Bad actor RJ Mitte dies aged 34: Mitte, who lived with cerebral palsy, starred as Walter White Jr in the Emmy-winning drama series.
- Six Ukrainian energy sites hit by Russia since Trump announced ceasefire, Zelensky says: Despite the US president announcing energy infrastructure would not be targeted strikes have continued, Ukraine says.
- The island where locals say data centres are taking their water: "Not a single drop has come through our taps for the last three months," a local tells the BBC.
- Watch: US man eyes pumpkin world record after fifth contest win: Horticulture teacher Travis Gienger hauled his pumpkin from Minnesota to Half Moon Bay, California where he won the annual event.
- South Africa's deputy police chief resigns after being charged with sexual offences: Shadrack Sibiya had denied grooming a 16-year-old and raping an 18-year-old.
- Immigration agents search congresswoman Ilhan Omar's home: Omar, an outspoken Trump critic, said the search was "an attempt to target political enemies" and she "will not be silenced".
- Bumble shares soar after report dating firm in $1bn takeover talks: The jump pushed Bumble's stock market valuation to more than $580m but that is still far below their peak of more than $14bn.
- Qantas flight grounded after bedbug outbreak: The flight from Italy to Australia was cancelled after passengers on the plane's previous journey complained of bug bites.
- Saudi minister vows 'serious response' to Houthi attacks on airports: It comes after the armed group hit Riyadh's international airport and another facility, killing 13 people, in a significant escalation.
- Fridges in French supermarkets hit by cyber attack: Hundreds of stores were targeted by the overnight hack, which spoiled fresh and frozen food estimated to be worth millions of euros.

image_provider.prompt: A broken, fractured landscape in deep blues and grays, with fissures running through earth and infrastructure—buildings tilted at wrong angles, power lines snapped, water pipes severed and dry. In the foreground, a single massive pumpkin sits pristine and untouched, glowing warm orange against the devastation, casting a stark shadow. Pixelated, bold shapes, high contrast, dystopian realism meets absurdist still life.
